newsitem.title: GERMANY: German EMU uncertainty weighs down bund futures.
newsitem.headline: German EMU uncertainty weighs down bund futures.

text.p: German bund futures ended markedly lower on Tuesday as concern that Germany would not meet the targets set for monetary union seeped through the market, sparked by comments from a Bundesbank council member.
Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said delay of European monetary union (EMU) was the only option if Germany did not strictly fulfil the criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.

He told a German magazine he saw little chance that Bonn would be able to cut its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product as required for entry to monetary union and that failure to do so would mean delaying EMU.
Dealers said the market was concerned that the prospect of Germany not meeting the criteria could lead to a weak European currency -- if the union went ahead on time.

They added that the closure of the March bund future at 99.99, 0.41 point down from Monday, was a negative sign for the market. A close above 100.20 would have indicated that the uptrend was still intact, one trader said.
But DG Bank said it believed the long-term uptrend remained in place. The bank said in a commentary "in our opinion the huge rise in yields does not signal a change in the interest rate trend."

"The positive factors for the bond market have barely changed," DG Bank added, commenting that the domestic growth outlook remained below the average potential level and that this meant there was no inflationary danger.
